title: `save_hyperparameters(ignore=...)` is not persistent across inheritance; ignored params reappear when base class also calls `save_hyperparameters`
author: aditya0by0

comments.author: CodeVishal-17
comments.body:
I’ve opened a PR that fixes this by making `save_hyperparameters(ignore=...)` persistent across inheritance and adding a regression test.

PR: #21489

comments.author: deependujha
comments.body:
Hi @aditya0by0, thanks for opening the issue. Also thanks @CodeVishal-17 for taking a look at it.

The fix imo is pretty simple:

https://github.com/Lightning-AI/pytorch-lightning/blob/79a39c04d37434f2234d9b518a145854d7c1e642/src/lightning/pytorch/core/mixins/hparams_mixin.py#L123-L124

when the function `save_hyperparameters()` is called, reset the previous hyperparameters.

```python
def save_hyperparameters(
        self,
        *args: Any,
        ignore: Optional[Union[Sequence[str], str]] = None,
        frame: Optional[types.FrameType] = None,
        logger: bool = True,
    ) -> None:

        # Reset hyperparameters before saving new ones
        self.hparams.clear()
        self._hparams.clear()

       ... # as it is
```

> [!NOTE]
> I'm in favour of: **`ignore` should not be persistent across inheritance, and the final child class should take absolute precedence**.

```python
import lightning as L

class Base(L.LightningModule):
    def __init__(self, a, b):
        super().__init__()
        self.save_hyperparameters()

class Child(Base):
    def __init__(self, a, b, c):
        super().__init__(a, b)
        self.save_hyperparameters(ignore="b")

def main():
    model = Child(1, 2, 3)
    print(model.hparams)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

Thoughts?

comments.author: aditya0by0
comments.body:
Yeah the approach looks clean, but the behavior would still be a bit inconsistent with how inheritance usually works or what user expects as flow of inheritance.

In your example, the child class will only ignore the parameters specified *at the child level*, while anything ignored in the base class is already lost and can’t be reconsidered. That means you end up storing “everything except the child’s ignored params”, rather than having a clean, inheritance-aware override.

Consider this case:

* `Base` ignores parameter `"a"`
* `Child` ignores parameter `"b"`

From an inheritance perspective,  I’d expect **only `"c"`** to be stored.

@deependujha, I might wrong about what the user expects. Please correct me.

comments.author: deependujha
comments.body:
Hi @aditya0by0, I see the concern, but this is also where I’m hesitant about making `ignore` persistent across inheritance.

`If ignores from the base class are automatically carried forward, then derived classes lose the ability to re-introduce those hyperparameters`. 
- That effectively makes base-class behavior irreversible, which is at odds with normal inheritance semantics where the most-derived class should have final authority.

In other words, persistence solves one problem (child ignores being re-added) but introduces another: *`there’s no way for a subclass to “unsubscribe” from what the base class chose to ignore`*.

---

My mental model is that **`derived classes override base classes`**. 
- If a base class wants to provide a default ignore list, it can expose it as an attribute and let subclasses reuse or modify it explicitly.

```python
import lightning as L

class Base(L.LightningModule):
    def __init__(self, a, b):
        super().__init__()
        self.ignore_list = ['b']
        self.save_hyperparameters(ignore=self.ignore_list)

class Child(Base):
    def __init__(self, a, b, c):
        super().__init__(a, b)
        self.ignore_list.append('c')
        self.save_hyperparameters(ignore=self.ignore_list)

def main():
    model = Child(1, 2, 3)
    print(model.hparams)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

Happy to hear your thoughts, especially if there’s a strong user expectation that ignores should compose transitively across inheritance.

comments.body:
I have updated the testcase, and the below scenario fails `arg5` is not stored in hparams. It is default param which  ignored in base class, but not in child class. 

``` python 
@pytest.mark.parametrize("ignore", ["arg2", ("arg2", "arg3")])
def test_hparams_ignore_in_subclass_overrides_base(tmp_path, ignore):
    """Test that hyperparameters can be ignored when `save_hyperparameters` is called in both a base class and a
    subclass, and that ignore rules defined in the subclass override hyperparameters saved by the base class."""

    class BaseBoringModel(BoringModel):
        def __init__(self, arg1, arg2, arg3, arg4=100, arg5=66):
            super().__init__()
            self.save_hyperparameters(ignore=("arg1", "arg5"))

    class LocalModel(BaseBoringModel):
        def __init__(self, arg1, arg2, arg3):
            super().__init__(arg1=arg1, arg2=arg2, arg3=arg3)
            self.save_hyperparameters(ignore=ignore)

    model = LocalModel(arg1=14, arg2=90, arg3=50)

    # `arg1` was ignored by the base class,
    # but the subclass did not ignore it, so it should be present.
    assert model.hparams.arg1 == 14
    assert model.hparams.arg4 == 100
    assert model.hparams.arg5 == 66
    ignore_args = ignore if isinstance(ignore, (list, tuple)) else [ignore]
    for arg in ignore_args:
        assert arg not in model.hparams
```

comments.author: deependujha
comments.body: arg5 was never passed as a hyperparameter to the derived class. It is expected.

comments.author: aditya0by0
comments.body:
Thats true, but I would expected the arg5 will be saved in checkpoint as per lightning behaviour before the change in the PR. 
But `arg5` doesnt't get stored in lightning checkpoint for the changes of our PR. If arg5 is not in hparams it doesn't get saved in checkpoint.

````python
    trainer = Trainer(default_root_dir=tmp_path, max_epochs=1, overfit_batches=0.5)
    trainer.fit(model)

    # make sure the raw checkpoint saved the properties
    raw_checkpoint_path = _raw_checkpoint_path(trainer)
    raw_checkpoint = torch.load(raw_checkpoint_path, weights_only=True)
    assert LightningModule.CHECKPOINT_HYPER_PARAMS_KEY in raw_checkpoint
    assert raw_checkpoint[LightningModule.CHECKPOINT_HYPER_PARAMS_KEY]["arg1"] == 14
    assert raw_checkpoint[LightningModule.CHECKPOINT_HYPER_PARAMS_KEY]["arg5"] == 66
```
